events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $4.41 (model confidence 0.85)
events.body:
RydeTAXI is metered, so extra kilometres enter the fare directly, and each off-route segment is audited separately for exemption [F1][F7][RD-1][RD-2][RD-3][RD-4][RD-5].

Segment F3 (21:42-21:49, +2.69 km): the trace marks the RD-4(a) screen ✓ — a DataMall accident on Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway, 0 m from the optimal route, reported 21:26, before this segment began [F12]. The driver's account matches it (accident ahead on KPE, lanes blocked) [F9], while the PAN ISLAND EXPRESSWAY record is only speed band 5, which is corroborative at best [F10][F11]. The segment is therefore exempt: no refund for its kilometres [F3][F12][RD-4].

Segment F4 (22:02-22:09, +3.13 km): the trace marks RD-4(a) ✗ — no qualifying incident covers this stretch, and a speed band alone does not exempt [F11][RD-4(b)(c)]. Nothing else excuses it. The chat record contains no rider message at all before the segment, so there is neither a rider-named stop nor any agreed route whose scope could be read [F8][RD-3(a)][RD-5]. The only assertion of agreement or justification is the driver's own after-the-trip statement, which is a claim, not the rider's consent and not a traffic record [F9][RD-4][RD-5]. The rider's complaint confirms no agreement to any change [F8]. The segment counts and is refundable [F3][F4][RD-1][RD-2].

Amount, using this trip's own rate from the fare record [F5][F7][RD-2]: $31.84 ÷ 22.58 km = $1.4101/km; the only non-exempt segment added 3.13 km [F4]; 3.13 km × $1.4101/km = $4.4136, rounded to $4.41. The trace confirms only segment-level extra km are refunded, not the residual excess-distance item [F5][RD-2].

No account flag: the driver profile shows 1 dispute, 1 upheld, but route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, so RD-6's repetition condition is not met, and profile facts cannot decide the case itself [F14][F15][RD-6]. Safety screen: the chat is empty, and the complaint and driver statement contain no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation — the only incident referenced is the third-party accident on KPE [F8][F9][F12][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: We reviewed your fare dispute and are refunding $4.41 as a Ryde voucher.

What decided it: part of your trip went off the route we'd expect, and the extra distance on that stretch (about 3 km between 10:02pm and 10:09pm) added to your metered fare. Another off-route stretch earlier in the trip was caused by a reported accident on the expressway and was left out of the refund. There was no record of a stop you asked for or a route change you agreed to on the refunded stretch.

The voucher is issued to your account. No action is needed on your side, and your account is not affected.

DRIVER: We reviewed a fare dispute on one of your trips and are refunding the rider $4.41 as a Ryde voucher.

What decided it: on one stretch (about 3 km between 10:02pm and 10:09pm), your route added distance with no reported incident and no message from the rider agreeing to a change. Your note about an agreed route wasn't supported by anything from the rider, so that segment's fare was refunded. A separate off-route stretch earlier was covered by a reported expressway accident and was not refunded.

No account flag was applied — no repeat issue was found. Please keep to the expected route or confirm any change with the rider in the app.

? RD-5 rider agreed to this route before the detour; scope of that agreement [F4] RULE: exempt only if a RIDER message sent before 22:02:05 agrees AND the agreement covers this segment. Three kinds of agreement: (1) GENERAL route choice ('take whichever way is faster') covers a route chosen to get there, not an errand of the driver's own (a stop away from the route, a loop that reaches nothing: counts). (2) A SPECIFIC named road or area ('go round via X') covers driving on X only: the record must tie this segment to X (a stop on X, a message placing the car on X, a road name in a fact); timing alone does not, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path — if nothing ties them, the finding is undetermined (G13); if the record places this segment somewhere else (a stop away from X, the driver's own statement naming another road or place, a stop the driver chose the location of), the agreement to X does not cover it: counts. (3) Scope unclear: undetermined. A driver's claim of agreement that appears only in his statement is not consent (G11); a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment: counts. This finding changes the amount. Evidence — F9: Driver statement (written after the trip, not part of the chat): “There was an accident on Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway ahead, lanes were blocked, so I went round it. The extra distance was unavoidable.” (F9)

notices.text:
We reviewed your fare dispute and are refunding $4.41 as a Ryde voucher.

What decided it: part of your trip went off the route we'd expect, and the extra distance on that stretch (about 3 km between 10:02pm and 10:09pm) added to your metered fare. Another off-route stretch earlier in the trip was caused by a reported accident on the expressway and was left out of the refund. There was no record of a stop you asked for or a route change you agreed to on the refunded stretch.

The voucher is issued to your account. No action is needed on your side, and your account is not affected.

We reviewed a fare dispute on one of your trips and are refunding the rider $4.41 as a Ryde voucher.

What decided it: on one stretch (about 3 km between 10:02pm and 10:09pm), your route added distance with no reported incident and no message from the rider agreeing to a change. Your note about an agreed route wasn't supported by anything from the rider, so that segment's fare was refunded. A separate off-route stretch earlier was covered by a reported expressway accident and was not refunded.

No account flag was applied — no repeat issue was found. Please keep to the expected route or confirm any change with the rider in the app.
